article_sentences: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath claimed the "80 versus 20" contest had returned, with 80 per cent of the electorate backing the NDA and 20 per cent with the opposition's PDA.

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday linked the latest Rajya Sabha contest in the state to the 2027 Assembly elections, saying it had set the tone for the bigger political battle ahead.
He claimed the “80 versus 20” contest had returned, with 80 per cent of the electorate backing the NDA and 20 per cent with the opposition’s PDA.
His remarks came a day after eight BJP candidates and two Samajwadi Party nominees filed papers for 10 Rajya Sabha seats from Uttar Pradesh.
With the SP not fielding a third candidate, all 10 nominees are set to be elected unopposed, subject to the completion of the electoral process.

Addressing the “Seva Jyoti Yatra-Viksit Bharat Sankalp Sabha” in Lucknow, Adityanath said, “The Rajya Sabha election (nominations) in Uttar Pradesh showed what the result of the Assembly election is going to be.
The 80 versus 20 fight has returned.
Eighty per cent are with the NDA and 20 per cent with the PDA, and what is going to happen to the PDA will again be before you.”
He had earlier said that 80 per cent of voters supported good governance under the BJP while 20 per cent would be on the opposite side.
SP chief Akhilesh Yadav had earlier hinted at fielding a third candidate.
But on the last date for filing nominations on Tuesday, he said his party’s focus was not on three seats but on the 403 Assembly seats in Uttar Pradesh.
Yadav had earlier said the party would field a third candidate once it had secured the required numbers.

article_sentences: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has claimed ownership over 50 cents of government poromboke land at Vilpatti village in Kodaikanal, falsely declared a property sold by him for ₹35 crore at Padi in Chennai as his property worth ₹7 crore and wrongly termed his Neelangarai bungalow as inherited property, an election petitioner has claimed before the Madras High Court.
However, Mr Vijay said the allegations against him were baseless and the petition must be dismissed.

In the petition pending before Justice V. Lakshminarayanan, S. Dinesh, a voter from Perambur constituency, insisted the election of the Chief Minister must be declared null and void for “wilful and deliberate” suppression, misrepresentation and false declarations with respect to many of the immovable properties referred to in his 2026 election affidavit.
According to the petitioner’s counsel V.R. Shanmuganathan, Mr. Vijay had claimed to have purchased the Vilpatti agricultural land for a consideration of ₹30,000 in 1997.
Mr Vijay had also said, the present market value of that property was around ₹20 lakh.
However, an examination of the village ‘A’ register revealed the property was actually a government poromboke land, the counsel claimed.
Similarly, the Chief Minister had declared to have purchased a non agricultural land measuring 33,955 square feet at Porur in Chennai for a consideration of ₹9.13 crore in 2010.
However, examination of registration department documents revealed that he had purchased only 20,773 square feet for ₹7.5 crore.
There was no explanation for excess declaration of the extent of the land as well as the sale amount, the petitioner alleged.

He went on to state that Mr. Vijay had declared to be owning a ₹7 crore worth 11,854 sq.ft commercial building at Padi in Chennai and claimed to have purchased it for a consideration of ₹1.95 crore in 2009 besides spending ₹3.9 crore on construction.
However, he had sold the commercial building with a constructed area of 23,460 sq.ft for a consideration of ₹35 crore on February 12, 2026, the petitioner claimed.

Further, the court was told he had not purchased the commercial property in 2009 as it had been declared in the election affidavit and instead received it in exchange for his Korattur property from Tamil Nadu Housing Board.

stories.headline: Trump: Covid crisis showed America’s dependence on China
stories.title: Trump: Covid crisis showed America’s dependence on China
stories.summary: Washington, Oct 7 : US President Donald Trump said that the Covid pandemic exposed America's dependence on China and other countries for critical products, arguing that the United States must rebuild domestic manufacturing capacity to protect its economic and national security. Trump says Covid exposed US reliance on China Speaking at Sparrows Point in Maryland, Trump linked his administration's push to expand American shipbuilding with a wider effort to bring strategic manufacturing back to the United States. “We learned that from COVID,” Trump said, referring to America's dependence on foreign suppliers. “We didn't make our farmers -- we didn't make our drugs, it was made in China and lots of other places, Ireland, all over Europe,” he said, according to a transcript of his remarks. Trump's comments came as he announced a major expansion of American shipbuilding capacity at the former industrial site outside Baltimore. The president has made reshoring manufacturing and reducing US dependence on foreign supply chains a central element of his economic and national-security agenda. He has particularly targeted America's economic relationship with China, using tariffs and other trade restrictions while pushing companies to manufacture more products in the United States. But Trump also said Tuesday that Washington continues to have an important economic relationship with Beijing. “We have a very good -- we've had -- always had a good relationship, but we're making a lot of money with China,” Trump said. Trump tied that approach to defence production, saying his administration had secured more than $76 billion in shipbuilding funding to produce more than 80 new vessels for the US Navy. The administration has argued that industrial capacity itself should be viewed as a national-security asset, particularly as the United States competes with China across military technology, advanced manufacturing and maritime power. At Sparrows Point, Trump and Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a new shipyard intended to manufacture submarine components and autonomous underwater vessels. The project brings together federal funding and private investment as Washington attempts to expand an industrial base that officials say has become too concentrated and unable to produce ships and submarines at the speed required by the military. Hegseth said the administration was seeking “speed, scale and urgency” from the Pentagon and defence companies. The strategy reflects a broader shift in US economic policy in which supply chains for semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, critical minerals, energy and defence equipment are increasingly viewed through the lens of national security. --IANS

stories.headline: RBI hikes repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5 pc; changes stance to 'calibrated tightening'
stories.title: RBI hikes repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5 pc; changes stance to 'calibrated tightening'
stories.summary: Mumbai, Oct 07: After nearly three-and-half years, the Reserve Bank of India on Wednesday raised key benchmark policy rate by 25 basis points to 5.5 per cent in a bid to tame rising inflation amid continuing West Asia crisis. With the rate hike, home loans, vehicle loans and corporate loans would become expensive and EMI for existing borrowers would also go up. A hike in the short-term lending rate (repo) by the RBI marks a reversal from its previous policy action. The last repo rate hike was in February 2023, when the RBI raised the rate by 0.25 per cent to 6.50 per cent. It kept the rate unchanged through 2023-24 before beginning its rate-cut cycle in 2025. Announcing the bi-monthly monetary policy, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) unanimously decided to raise the policy repo rate by 25 basis points. Meanwhile, retail inflation rose to 4.82 per cent in August as compared to 4.45 per cent in the previous month. MPC changed its stance to 'calibrated tightening' from 'neutral' and also underscored that rate cut is unlikely in the near term given the current conditions. Besides, MPC must have taken into account the recent actions by central banks of developed nations especially the US Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank. Last month, the US Fed effected a 25 basis points rate hike to rein in inflation brought on by spiralling oil prices and other factors. Prior to the Fed, the European Central Bank too raised its key interest rate by 25 basis points.

stories.summary: India-U.S. trade talks have hit a “plateau”, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman tells India Today Global, with both sides finding the remaining give-and-take increasingly difficult. Sitharaman also says tariffs have become “weaponised” as Washington seeks to address its trade imbalance. At the centre of the dispute are tariffs, market access, agriculture and dairy, sensitive sectors, non-tariff barriers and India’s continued purchase of Russian crude. Sitharaman argues that India’s energy choices should not become a bargaining chip in trade negotiations, while also pointing to the different approach taken by Europe. The big question: Is Washington negotiating with India — or using tariff pressure to push for a deal on U.S. terms? India says it remains committed to deeper economic ties with America, but wants reciprocal concessions and room to protect its farmers, sensitive sectors and strategic interests.

article_sentences: The six-member Monetary Policy Committee voted unanimously to raise the repo rate, the first such increase since Governor Sanjay Malhotra took office in December 2024.

The Reserve Bank of India raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% on Wednesday, its first increase in nearly four years, and signalled that further hikes could follow as rising inflation and a weakening currency prompt a policy pivot.
The six-member Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) voted unanimously to raise the repo rate, the first such increase since Governor Sanjay Malhotra took office in December 2024.
While the move was widely expected, the central bank sprang a surprise in shifting its stance towards "calibrated tightening", effectively ruling out a rate cut in the near term.

"Rate cuts are off the table in the near term and policy action ahead can only be a rate hike or a pause, depending on the evolving conditions and the outlook," Malhotra said announcing the MPC decisions.

The governor, however, cautioned that the timing and extent of any further tightening would depend on the evolution of inflation and growth, particularly underlying price pressures and the extent to which supply shocks become embedded in the broader economy.
With the decision, India has joined major central banks in raising rates as higher oil prices triggered by the Iran war fuel inflation, squeeze purchasing power and weigh on currencies.
Compounding the price pressures is weak rains linked to El Nino.
Inflation pressures have broadened even as economic activity remains resilient.
Consumer-price inflation rose to 4.82% in August, above the RBI's 4% medium-term target for a third consecutive month, while core inflation accelerated to 4.2%.

The central bank said inflation risks were no longer as benign as they had been a year earlier, pointing to higher food and fuel prices, deficient monsoon rainfall, El Nino conditions, and renewed volatility in international oil prices.
The RBI now expects headline inflation to average 5.2% in the 2026-27 financial year, with inflation projected to rise to 6.0% in the third quarter and 5.7% in the fourth quarter.

stories.headline: US spice industry seeks lower tariffs on Indian spice imports
stories.title: US spice industry seeks lower tariffs on Indian spice imports
stories.summary: Washington, Oct 7 : The US spice industry is seeking continued tariff exemptions for Indian spices and wants the protection made permanent as Washington and New Delhi move towards a trade agreement, arguing that many of the products cannot be grown commercially in the United States. Donald Pratt, president of the American Spice Trade Association (ASTA), said the industry's priority was to preserve tariff exemptions for agricultural products unavailable domestically but widely used by American consumers and businesses. “Well, for our industry, it's about the continued exemption, you know, from tariffs, of agriculture that's not grown in this hemisphere and cannot be grown in this hemisphere, but that is beloved by our consumers, you know, and our business partners, worldwide,” Pratt told IANS at an event at India House in Washington. Pratt said the Indian Embassy and others involved in the negotiations had already undertaken significant advocacy on the issue. “But also I think as they go to wrap up the next phase of that, we hope that that continues the exemption now that we're seeing and becomes hopefully permanently, you know, enshrined, you know, as an exception to tariffs,” he said. Pratt's comments put a spotlight on a segment of India-US commerce in which the American industry argues imports are essential because domestic production cannot meet demand. Addressing the gathering separately, Pratt said India grows more than half of the 109 spices recognised by the International Organization for Standardization and is an essential supplier to the US industry. The United States is the largest market for Indian spices, importing about $700 million worth last year, according to figures cited by Pratt. “Here's the reality for our industry. The United States grows only a small fraction of the spices we use. Many spices simply can't be grown here at scale,” he said. Pratt said the industry had spent considerable effort explaining why spices should be treated differently when tariffs were being considered. He said there was now greater recognition that many spices are tied to particular climates and growing conditions and cannot simply be replaced with US production. “So we rely on India for cumin, fennel, chilies, and dozens more spices,” he said. “They season the food Americans enjoy every day.” Pratt said ASTA had worked closely with the Indian Embassy on tariffs over the past 18 months and described those discussions as “open, practical, collaborative”. The association also mounted its own campaign to keep spices outside new tariff barriers. “Asta led the industry advocacy for spices to be exempt from new, tariffs,” Pratt said. “Our advocacy paid off last year with most spices included on exemption lists for Section 122 as well as 301 tariffs as unavailable natural resources,” he said. “And as India and the US move towards a final trade agreement, we're hopeful for further considerations that keep spices accessible and affordable.” The industry's case is built partly around the argument that tariffs on spices unavailable in the United States would raise costs without providing protection to a significant competing domestic industry. Roberto Fanni, who chairs ASTA's science and regulatory committee, said the association had secured exemptions for spices because the United States was not a major producer. He told, “However, spices are exempt because it's recognized that US is not a producer of spices, so there is no any national production that can be, I would say pushed if there is a ban or there are tariffs for spices,” Fanni said the relationship between suppliers in India and the US market was also evolving, with Indian producers increasingly understanding American requirements. “The spice trace is definitely strategic. It's growing and it's really amazing to see how the relationship between the two countries are getting better,” he said. He said suppliers and producers in India were addressing food safety and compliance issues from the farm level to make products more readily acceptable in the United States and allow trade volumes to expand. Laura Schumer, executive director of the American Spice Trade Association, said India occupies a central position in the industry's supply chain. “India is absolutely our most critical trade partner,” Schumer told IANS. “Historically, we've relied so heavily on India, both for the breadth of spices, the volume of spices, and the value of spices that we import into the United States. India is our most critical trade partner, bar none.” Schumer said the association represents about 100 companies that import, process, manufacture and sell spices in the United States. The India House event brought industry members together with government representatives and organisations working across the food and agriculture supply chain. India and the United States have a broad trade relationship spanning goods and services, with tariffs and market access among the issues that have periodically produced differences between the two sides. Agriculture is particularly sensitive because trade policy can directly affect domestic producers, importers and consumers. The spice industry's position distinguishes products that can be produced domestically from those that cannot be grown commercially in the United States. ASTA's case is that exempting unavailable natural resources such as many spices allows American businesses to maintain supplies without undermining comparable US agricultural production. --IANS

stories.title: Rupee falls 10 paise to 96.45 against US dollar ahead of RBI monetary policy decision
stories.summary: Mumbai, Oct 07: The rupee depreciated 10 paise to 96.45 against the US dollar in early trade on Wednesday ahead of the Reserve Bank of India's monetary policy decision. The rupee is under continuous pressure amid persistent outflows of foreign funds from domestic equities and strong US dollar holding near multi-month highs above 102 (DXY), forex traders said. Moreover, investors are keenly awaiting the RBI's monetary policy decision for further cues. At the interbank foreign exchange, the rupee opened at 96.37, then lost ground and fell to 96.45, down 10 paise from its previous close. On Tuesday, the rupee settled at 96.35 against the US dollar. "We have the RBI monetary policy meeting today, in which the RBI is expected to raise rates by 25 bps with an outside chance of a 50 bps raise. The RBI may also raise the CRR by 1 per cent to 4 per cent to absorb the excess liquidity. "We await the RBI stance on the falling rupee which has lost more than 2 per cent in the last 1 month with oil demand and FPI demand for the US dollar keeping the rupee lower," said Anil Kumar Bhansali, Head of Treasury and Executive Director, Finrex Treasury Advisors LLP, said. The Reserve Bank of India will announce its bi-monthly monetary policy decision at 1000 hrs on Wednesday, with several experts expecting a rate hike after nearly three-and-a-half years as inflation pressures rise due to the continuing West Asia conflict. The RBI last hiked the repo rate in February 2023, raising it by 0.25 per cent to 6.50 per cent. It kept the rate unchanged through 2023-24 before beginning its rate-cut cycle in 2025. The RBI's policy repo rate currently stands at 5.25 per cent. Meanwhile, the dollar index, which gauges the strength of the greenback against a basket of six currencies, was trading at 102.02, higher by 0.19 per cent. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was trading higher by 0.91 per cent at USD 101.50 per barrel in futures trade. On the domestic equity market front, Sensex fell 460 points to 72,599.05 in early trade, while the Nifty declined 164.80 points to 22,610.85. Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) offloaded equities worth Rs 2,961.30 crore on a net basis on Tuesday, according to exchange data.

stories.headline: Inox Green Completes ₹550 Cr Acquisition of WWIL’s 4.5 GW Wind O&M Business
stories.title: Inox Green Completes ₹550 Cr Acquisition of WWIL’s 4.5 GW Wind O&M Business
stories.summary: Inox Green Energy Solutions Limited (Inox Green), part of the INOXGFL Group, has completed the ₹550-crore payment to acquire Wind World India Limited’s (WWIL) wind O&M business. In a press release, Inox Green, a listed renewable energy operations and maintenance (O&M) service provider, said it made the payment under a Business Transfer Agreement (BTA) through its subsidiary Vibhav Energy Pvt Ltd (VEPL). Under the agreement, WWIL’s O&M business will be transferred to VEPL as a going concern. As per the terms of the BTA and the Resolution Plan approved by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), Inox Green will hold a 75% stake in VEPL after the business transfer and implementation of the Resolution Plan is completed. This will enable Inox Green to consolidate the transferred business’s financials on a line-by-line basis. Supported by the broader INOXGFL Group ecosystem—including planned large annual capacity additions at Inox Clean Energy and external projects executed by parent company Inox Wind—Inox Green said it is firmly on track to exceed 20 GW of serviced capacity in the near future. WWIL’s 4.5 GW Portfolio WWIL’s 4.5 GW O&M portfolio includes a marquee client base comprising the Tata Group, ReNew, Greenko Group, Apraava Energy, and Hindustan Zinc. The assets are spread across key wind-rich states, including Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Andhra Pradesh. The portfolio generated approximately ₹580 crore in revenue in FY26 and benefits from contracted annual price escalation of approximately 5%. Following the transaction, Inox Green’s O&M portfolio stands at approximately 13.3 GWp as of June 2026, inclusive of WWIL’s portfolio and a separate approximately 2 GW wind O&M acquisition currently held as an investment. Inox Green said it expects to leverage operational efficiencies, advanced technology platforms, and group synergies to substantially increase the acquired portfolio’s revenues and operating margins. Commenting on the acquisition, Devansh Jain, Executive Director, INOXGFL Group, said, “This transaction will be a defining step in our strategy to build India’s largest and most technologically advanced renewable energy services platform. Wind World’s quality asset base and deeply entrenched customer relationships complement Inox Green’s strengths and reinforce our long-term growth ambitions. “The transaction substantially enhances our multi-brand OEM O&M capabilities and strengthens our ability to deliver superior operational performance across a larger fleet of wind assets.” Jain added, “We are now focused on a seamless integration of Wind World India’s O&M business, leveraging our combined capabilities to drive greater value for customers, accelerate growth and further consolidate our leadership in the renewable energy services sector.” Akhil Jindal, Group CFO, INOXGFL Group, said, “We are extremely pleased to announce that this milestone transaction has been executed within our disciplined valuation framework. The business has several synergistic opportunities and the transaction multiple works out to approximately 2x EBITDA, based on expected earnings after the full realisation of synergies over the next year. “As we integrate the acquired business, our focus will be on driving operational efficiencies, improving margins and unlocking synergies to maximize value creation.”

stories.headline: SC expresses displeasure over Rajpal Yadav’s conduct in cheque cases
stories.title: SC expresses displeasure over Rajpal Yadav’s conduct in cheque cases
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 7 : The Supreme Court on Wednesday directed actor and comedian Rajpal Yadav to deposit Rs 1.15 crore with the apex court registry after his counsel submitted that the amount was ready to be deposited immediately, while another Rs 85 lakh would be arranged through a prospective buyer of his ancestral property, as part of arrangements to pay Rs 2 crore in connection with multiple cheque dishonour cases. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana was hearing Yadav and his wife Radha Yadav's pleas challenging the Delhi High Court judgment upholding their conviction in seven cheque dishonour cases under the Negotiable Instruments Act. During the hearing, the CJI Kant-led Bench was informed that Yadav had arranged Rs 1.15 crore through demand drafts, while a prospective buyer of his ancestral property, who was present in court, was willing to pay another Rs 85 lakh as an advance. Yadav’s counsel told the top court that the buyer was not presently willing to register the sale documents due to Pitru Paksha and wanted to proceed with the registration after the commencement of Navratri. The counsel further submitted that the buyer was willing to deposit the Rs 85 lakh by way of a demand draft on Monday. However, the Supreme Court questioned the overall value of the transaction, remarking that the liability was substantially higher than Rs 2 crore. "What will be the total sale consideration? Because the liability is much more than Rs 2 crore," the CJI Kant-led Bench asked. The counsel said the property was valued at more than Rs 30 crore and confirmed that the prospective buyer had the capacity to make the proposed payment. The complainant's counsel agreed to the proposal and submitted that if Rs 2 crore was paid immediately, Yadav could be granted additional time to pay the remaining amount. A bench of Justice KV Viswanathan and Justice Arun Palli was hearing a Special Leave Petition (SLP) when it came heavily on the state government, observing that “grave injustice has been done to the petitioner.”

stories.title: Bharti Airtel raises postpaid tariffs - Will Jio, Vodafone Idea follow? A look back at previous trends
stories.summary: With the massive 5G capital deployment cycle which is now peaking, according to Equirus, the industry requires another systemic pricing intervention to protect long-term returns, the firm wrote in its note.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: "One blinks, others follow within days." That is Equirus Securities' summarization of past tariff hikes taken by telecom operators over the last decade.
Equirus highlighted this while initiating coverage on the telecom companies back on September 28.
This assumes greater significance now that Bharti Airtel has gone ahead and increased its postpaid tariff plans by ₹50 across the board.
Postpaid currently contributes between 8% to 12% of Bharti Airtel's topline, according to industry estimates.
The key question now comes to mind is, with Bharti having made the move, will both Jio and Vodafone Idea follow suit?
Equirus analyses these past patterns.

Calling it a move to "survive" and not "grow", Equirus highlighted how Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea rolled out their precise plan details on December 1, 2019, and implementing those from December 3.
Three days later, Reliance Jio implemented its "All-in-One" plan.
Tariffs were raised between 20% to 40% and operators reworked their 28-day, 84-day and 365-day plans.
As a result of this tariff hike, Bharti Airtel's Average Revenue Per User (ARPU) jumped from ₹135 in the third quarter of financial year 2020 to ₹166 in the third quarter of financial year 2021.
Reliance Jio saw a similar jump from ₹128 to ₹151, while Vodafone Idea's ARPU increased from ₹109 to ₹121 during the same timeframe.
Two years later, in November 2021, Bharti Airtel once again took the lead in announcing a 20% to 25% blanket increase across all prepaid plans, which took effect from November 26 that year.

stories.headline: Union Ministers laud Modi’s 25-year journey in government
stories.title: Union Ministers laud Modi’s 25-year journey in government
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 7 : As Prime Minister Narendra Modi completed 25 years as the head of government, Union Ministers on Wednesday hailed his leadership, saying he has transformed the very definition of governance through people-centric policies, effective implementation, firm decision-making, transparency and a focus on results, while establishing the ideal of the 'politics of performance'. Prime Minister Narendra Modi completed 25 years as head of government, marking a political journey that began with his appointment as Gujarat Chief Minister on October 7, 2001, and continued with three consecutive terms as Prime Minister since 2014. Union Home Minister Amit Shah took to the social media platform X and wrote in Hindi, “Heartfelt congratulations to the illustrious Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji on completing 25 years of his service and dedication, characterised by tireless hard work, remarkable resolve and making the nation first the goal of life.” “On this very day, October 7, 2001, Modi ji took oath as the Chief Minister of Gujarat. Since then, his continuous journey of service, struggle and dedication as Chief Minister and Prime Minister has become synonymous with the welfare of the poor, empowerment of women, upliftment of youth and prosperity of every section of society,” he said. “In 25 years of Seva, Modi ji has transformed the very definition of governance through people-centric policies, their implementation, firmness in decision-making, transparency and a guarantee of results, while establishing the ideal of ‘politics of performance’,” HM Shah said. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said, “Today marks 25 years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s journey in public service. Having served as the Chief Minister of Gujarat for 13 years and as the Prime Minister of India for the past 12 years, Modi ji has remained steadfastly dedicated to the service of the people. I extend my heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to him on this remarkable journey.” “His journey, which began on October 7, 2001, as the Chief Minister of Gujarat, has come to symbolise nation-building, good governance and public welfare. The guiding principle throughout this journey has always been ‘Nation First, Always First’,” he said. “Under Modi ji’s visionary leadership, welfare initiatives have expanded on an unprecedented scale, enabling crores of people to gain access to basic necessities such as homes, tap water, toilets, LPG connections and banking services,” Singh added. “Today, guided by the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat’, we are moving forward with the resolve to build a ‘Viksit Bharat’. Under the leadership of Modi ji, good governance has been strengthened, and India has steadily advanced towards self-reliance across sectors,” he said. “Today, we have emerged as the world’s fourth-largest economy, while the benefits of development have become more inclusive. Employment and opportunities for our youth have expanded, entrepreneurship and startups have received a strong impetus, and new avenues for innovation have opened up. At the same time, India is strengthening its internal security and responding to external threats with firmness and resolve,” Rajnath Singh added. “The 25-year journey of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in the service of the nation is an inspiration for all of us. These 25 years mark a milestone in his journey, not a full stop. My best wishes are that, in the years ahead, we continue to move forward on the path of national service with renewed energy and dedication, under his visionary leadership, guided by the resolve that ‘Jan Seva is Prabhu Seva’ - service to the people is service to the Almighty,” he said. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman also hailed PM Modi and said, “Today, October 7, we celebrate the chequered career of PM Narendra Modi. Twenty-five years ago, on this day, he took up the responsibility of Chief Minister of Gujarat. Until then, he had held no elected post. Through dedication, he served, learning as he went along. Selfless, no corruption, no cronies. Now, he serves as Prime Minister. Only in the BJP, a karyakarta gets opportunities despite having no political family or dynastic background, money, etc. A strong message for democracy.” Education Minister Pralhad Joshi said, “A remarkable journey of 25 years in public service, defined by decisive leadership, tireless dedication and an unwavering commitment to the people of India. From Gujarat to the national stage, Hon’ble PM Shri Narendra Modi ji has remained steadfast in his resolve to serve Bharat and build a stronger, more prosperous and Viksit Bharat. A journey of Seva, Sankalp and Nation First that continues to inspire.” Union Minister Giriraj Singh extended heartfelt congratulations and said, “Heartfelt congratulations to the Honourable Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji on this significant journey of 25 years in public life. In these years, your leadership has created a distinct identity by placing service, resolve and national interest at the centre of public life. Your dedication to the country and unwavering commitment serve as an inspiration to millions of Indians. May God grant you excellent health, and may this journey of national service continue to progress with the same energy.” Union Minister Nitin Gadkari said, “Thank you PM Shri Narendra Modi ji for 25 years of fearless and focused leadership. There were many moments when the easy way was available, but you always chose the right way, even when it was difficult. That kind of courage is rare.” Union Minister Piyush Goyal described the occasion as “25 years of relentless devotion to Maa Bharati and her people”. --IANS

Prime Minister Narendra Modi completed 25 years as head of government, marking a political journey that began with his appointment as Gujarat Chief Minister on October 7, 2001, and continued with three consecutive terms as Prime Minister since 2014.
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said, “Today marks 25 years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s journey in public service.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah took to the social media platform X and wrote in Hindi, “Heartfelt congratulations to the illustrious Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji on completing 25 years of his service and dedication, characterised by tireless hard work, remarkable resolve and making the nation first the goal of life.”
